name: Uber-anatomy Ontology
description: A cross-species anatomy ontology covering animals, with extensive coverage of nervous system structures. It is the common anatomy backbone for many cell, expression and phenotype resources.

publications.title: Uberon, an integrative multi-species anatomy ontology

usedBy.name: HuBMAP
usedBy.note: Anatomical structures in the Human Reference Atlas

name: Foundational Model of Anatomy
description: A detailed reference ontology of human anatomy, including fine-grained neuroanatomy. Marked inactive in the OBO Foundry; much of its neuro content is cross-referenced from Uberon.
maintainer: University of Washington Structural Informatics Group

publications.title: A reference ontology for biomedical informatics: the Foundational Model of Anatomy

name: Allen Mouse Brain Atlas Ontology
description: The hierarchy of adult mouse brain regions used by the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas and Common Coordinate Framework, packaged as an OWL ontology by the BICAN community.

name: Developing Mouse Brain Atlas Ontology
description: Brain region hierarchy of the Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas, covering embryonic and postnatal stages.

name: Human Brain Atlas Ontology
description: Adult human brain region hierarchy from the Allen Human Brain Atlas, packaged as an OWL ontology.

name: Developing Human Brain Atlas Ontology
description: Brain region hierarchy of the developing human brain, as used by BrainSpan and the Allen developing human atlases.

usedBy.name: BrainSpan
usedBy.note: Region annotation of developmental transcriptome data

name: NeuroNames
description: A long-standing nomenclature of primate brain structures with synonyms across languages and atlases, served through BrainInfo.

publications.title: NeuroNames: an ontology for the BrainInfo portal to neuroscience on the web

name: Zebrafish Anatomy Ontology
description: Anatomy and development of the zebrafish, including the larval and adult nervous system.

name: Drosophila Anatomy Ontology
description: Anatomy of Drosophila melanogaster, including thousands of named neuron types linked to connectome datasets.

publications.title: The Drosophila anatomy ontology

name: C. elegans Gross Anatomy Ontology
description: Anatomy of Caenorhabditis elegans, including every identified neuron of its 302-neuron nervous system.

name: Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework
description: A 3D reference space for the adult mouse brain with annotated regions at 10 µm resolution. The de facto standard for registering mouse brain data.

publications.title: The Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework: A 3D Reference Atlas

name: Waxholm Space Atlas of the Sprague Dawley Rat Brain
description: An open, MRI/DTI-based volumetric atlas and reference space for the rat brain with delineated regions.

publications.title: Waxholm Space atlas of the Sprague Dawley rat brain

name: Julich-Brain Cytoarchitectonic Atlas
description: Probabilistic cytoarchitectonic maps of the human brain, available through EBRAINS and the siibra toolsuite.

publications.title: Julich-Brain: A 3D probabilistic atlas of the human brain's cytoarchitecture

name: Cell Ontology
description: The reference ontology of cell types across organisms, with a large and growing branch of neuron and glial types.

publications.title: The Cell Ontology 2016: enhanced content, modularization, and ontology interoperability

usedBy.name: BIDS
usedBy.note: Recommended vocabulary for the CellType metadata field

name: Provisional Cell Ontology
description: Holds data-driven cell types (e.g. from single-cell transcriptomics of the brain) before they are ready for the Cell Ontology, linked to their source taxonomies.

name: Neuron Phenotype Ontology
description: Defines neuron types by combinations of phenotypes (location, morphology, molecular markers, electrophysiology, projections). Part of the NIF Ontology.

publications.title: The Neuron Phenotype Ontology: A FAIR Approach to Proposing and Classifying Neuronal Types

name: Cell Annotation Schema
description: A JSON Schema for recording cell type annotations of single-cell datasets, including evidence, marker genes and links to ontology terms.

tools.name: Taxonomy Development Tools
tools.note: Build and edit Cell Annotation Schema taxonomies

name: Common Cell Type Nomenclature
description: A convention for naming and identifying data-driven cell types and taxonomies so that they can be compared and tracked across studies.

publications.title: Common cell type nomenclature for the mammalian brain

name: Neuro Behavior Ontology
description: Covers behavioral processes and phenotypes, such as learning, motor and social behavior, for annotating animal and human behavior.

name: Cognitive Atlas
description: A collaborative knowledge base of cognitive concepts, tasks, and the relations between them, built for annotating cognitive neuroscience experiments.

publications.title: The Cognitive Atlas: Toward a Knowledge Foundation for Cognitive Neuroscience

usedBy.name: NeuroVault
usedBy.note: Tagging statistical maps with cognitive tasks

name: Cognitive Paradigm Ontology
description: Describes the stimuli, instructions and responses that make up cognitive experimental paradigms in neuroimaging studies.

publications.title: The Cognitive Paradigm Ontology: Design and Application

name: Mental Functioning Ontology
description: Represents mental functioning, including mental processes such as cognition and traits such as intelligence.

name: Emotion Ontology
description: Represents affective phenomena such as emotions, moods and appraisals, as an extension of the Mental Functioning Ontology.

name: Mental Disease Ontology
description: Describes and categorises mental disorders, built on the Mental Functioning Ontology.

name: Mondo Disease Ontology
description: A unified disease ontology that merges many disease resources, with comprehensive coverage of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders.

publications.title: Mondo: Unifying diseases for the world, by the world

name: Human Phenotype Ontology
description: Standard vocabulary of phenotypic abnormalities in human disease, with a large nervous system abnormality branch used in rare-disease diagnostics.

publications.title: The Human Phenotype Ontology in 2021

name: Alzheimer's Disease Ontology
description: Covers the clinical, preclinical and molecular knowledge domains of Alzheimer's disease.

publications.title: ADO: a disease ontology representing the domain knowledge specific to Alzheimer's disease

name: Neurological Disease Ontology
description: A framework for representing neurological diseases together with their diagnosis, treatment and associated clinical findings.

name: Epilepsy and Seizure Ontology
description: Represents epilepsy syndromes, seizure types, EEG findings and treatments, aligned with ILAE classifications.

name: Parkinson's Disease Ontology
description: Models knowledge about Parkinson's disease, including etiology, symptoms, diagnosis and treatment, for literature mining and data integration.

name: Gene Ontology
description: Describes gene product functions, processes and locations, including synaptic transmission, neurotransmitter release and neuron development.

publications.title: The Gene Ontology knowledgebase in 2023

usedBy.name: SynGO
usedBy.note: Synaptic annotations built on GO terms

name: SynGO – Synaptic Gene Ontologies and Annotations
description: Expert-curated, evidence-based annotations of synaptic gene functions and locations, organised with Gene Ontology terms.

publications.title: SynGO: An Evidence-Based, Expert-Curated Knowledge Base for the Synapse

name: Chemical Entities of Biological Interest
description: An ontology of small molecules, including neurotransmitters, neuromodulators and neuroactive drugs, with their chemical roles.

publications.title: ChEBI in 2016: Improved services and an expanding collection of metabolites

name: Brain Imaging Data Structure
description: A community standard for organising and describing neuroimaging and related data: MRI, EEG, MEG, iEEG, PET, microscopy, NIRS, motion, MRS, EMG, eye tracking, and derivatives such as atlases. Its rules are a machine-readable YAML schema, also exported as one JSON file, that renders the specification and drives the BIDS Validator. Metadata fields point to HED, Cognitive Atlas, CogPO, the Cell Ontology, NCBI Taxonomy and RRIDs.

publications.title: The brain imaging data structure, a format for organizing and describing outputs of neuroimaging experiments
The past, present, and future of the brain imaging data structure (BIDS)
EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
iEEG-BIDS, extending the Brain Imaging Data Structure specification to human intracranial electrophysiology
MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
PET-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for positron emission tomography
The genetics-BIDS extension: Easing the search for genetic data associated with human brain imaging
Microscopy-BIDS: An Extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure for Microscopy Data
qMRI-BIDS: An extension to the brain imaging data structure for quantitative magnetic resonance imaging data
ASL-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extension for arterial spin labeling
NIRS-BIDS: Brain Imaging Data Structure Extended to Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
Motion-BIDS: an extension to the brain imaging data structure to organize motion data for reproducible research
MRS-BIDS, an extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure for magnetic resonance spectroscopy

publications.title: Sharing brain mapping statistical results with the neuroimaging data model

name: Hierarchical Event Descriptors
description: A structured vocabulary and annotation system for describing experimental events in time-series data such as EEG, MEG, fMRI and behavior.

publications.title: Building FAIR Functionality: Annotating Events in Time Series Data Using Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED)

name: Neural ElectroMagnetic Ontologies
description: Ontologies for event-related potential (ERP) data and analysis in EEG and MEG studies. A legacy resource.

name: Neurodata Without Borders Schema
description: A data standard and schema for neurophysiology: extracellular and intracellular electrophysiology, optical physiology, behavior and stimuli, extensible via neurodata extensions (NDX).

publications.title: The Neurodata Without Borders ecosystem for neurophysiological data science

name: odML Terminologies
description: Terminologies for the odML metadata format, giving standard keys for describing electrophysiology experiments, subjects and hardware.

publications.title: A Bottom-up Approach to Data Annotation in Neurophysiology

name: NeuroML
description: An XML-based language (with XSD schema) for describing detailed neuron, synapse and network models in a simulator-independent way.

publications.title: NeuroML: a language for describing data driven models of neurons and networks with a high degree of biological detail

name: Computational Neuroscience Ontology
description: A controlled vocabulary of terms used to describe and annotate computational neuroscience models. A legacy resource.

name: openMINDS
description: A set of metadata models and controlled terms for neuroscience graph databases, covering datasets, subjects, methods, software, models and brain atlases (SANDS).

description: A JSON-LD schema for standardising assessments and questionnaires, with versioned items, scoring and provenance, plus a shared library of instruments.

name: Neuroshapes
description: Open SHACL schemas for neuroscience data and provenance, originally developed within INCF and used by Blue Brain Nexus.

name: SPARC Dataset Structure
description: File and metadata structure for datasets in the NIH SPARC programme on the peripheral nervous system, with curation tooling that maps to InterLex terms.

name: NIF Standard Ontology
description: The Neuroscience Information Framework ontology: a broad, modular set of neuroscience terms spanning anatomy, cells, molecules, techniques and resources.

publications.title: The NIFSTD and BIRNLex Vocabularies: Building Comprehensive Ontologies for Neuroscience

name: InterLex
description: A dynamic term registry (successor to NeuroLex) where neuroscience terms are minted, linked to existing ontologies and given stable ILX identifiers.

name: Brain Architecture Management System
description: A knowledge management system for nervous system structure and connectivity data, with its own brain region nomenclatures. A legacy resource.

name: Primate Brain Atlas Ontology
description: An application ontology of the Allen Institute Primate Brain Atlas structure graph, mapped to Uberon. Currently in draft status.

name: Harmonized Ontology of Mammalian Brain Anatomy
description: A BICAN ontology that harmonizes brain anatomy terms across mammalian brain atlases. Built with the Ontology Development Kit; early-stage.

name: Spinal Cord Atlas Ontology
description: An early-stage BICAN ontology repository for spinal cord atlas structures, set up with the Ontology Development Kit.

name: BICAN Application Ontology
description: An application ontology covering research, research subjects and research results in BICAN, linking experimental knowledge to how data is distributed. It builds on earlier BICCN and Brain Data Standards work.

name: BICAN Techniques Ontology
description: An ontology of experimental techniques and methods used across the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network, to help scientists describe how data were produced.

name: BICAN Metadata Schemas
description: Metadata schemas and curation documentation for BICAN data, each reviewed and standardized by the BICAN Metadata and Ontologies Integration Working Group (MOWG).

name: Addiction Ontology
description: An ontology being developed to cover all aspects of addiction research. It imports from, and is reused by, the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology (BCIO).

name: Neuroimaging Informatics Technology Initiative format
description: The standard file format for volumetric neuroimaging data. A fixed binary header (NIfTI-1, or NIfTI-2 for large dimensions) carries voxel-to-world affines (qform/sform), units, intent codes and extensions, followed by the image array. Defined by the NIfTI Data Format Working Group; CIFTI-2 builds on NIfTI-2 for grayordinate data.

name: Psych-DS
description: A BIDS-inspired standard for organising datasets from psychological and behavioural research (experiments, surveys, assessments): CSV data files with keyword-formatted names and dataset metadata in schema.org JSON-LD. What counts as valid is defined by a versioned YAML schema model that the Psych-DS validators read.

name: Neuroscience Information Exchange format
description: A generic data model and HDF5-based file format, started in the INCF Electrophysiology Task Force, that stores neuroscience data (time series, images, events, regions of interest) together with their metadata in one container. Metadata follow the odML model, and Neo reads and writes NIX files.

name: Neurobagel data model and vocabulary
description: An RDF vocabulary (nb:) and a JSON Schema for data dictionaries that harmonise participant-level metadata (age, sex, diagnosis, assessments, imaging modality, processing pipelines) by annotating BIDS participants.tsv columns with SNOMED CT, NCIt and NIDM terms. The resulting graphs power Neurobagel's federated search across datasets.

name: NeuroBlueprint
description: A lightweight, BIDS-inspired specification for organising systems-neuroscience project folders by subject, session and datatype (ephys, behav, funcimg, anat) from acquisition onward. Developed by the Neuroinformatics Unit at the Sainsbury Wellcome Centre and implemented by datashuttle.
